newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dollars to slow won's fall.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dollars to slow won's fall.

text.p: The Bank of Korea stepped into Seoul's interbank market in early Wednesday trading by selling dollars to slow the won's decline, dealers said.
The central bank denied its intervention.
The won opened trading at the 83-month low of 853.00 per dollar and soon rebounded to 852.60 after the intervention, they said.
Dealers said the won was under downward pressure by the nation's widening trade deficit and the Japanese yen's weakness against the dollar in world markets.
The dollar was steady at above 118 yen in early Tokyo trading.
Wednesday's opening rate was lower than Tuesday's closing rate of 852.80 and was the lowest level since the nation introduced market-average system in March 1990.
